MIND. [1] [Chin. s.]
Indifference, stupid expression, vacant stare, averse to answering questions. θ Typhus.
Great mental depression. θ Variola.
Despondency.
Semi-consciousness, she is partly insensible to pain. θ Spinal irritation.
Unconsciousness. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Unconsciousness, with red face, deep and noisy respiration, pulse full and very slow, recurring every other day at same hour. θ Intermittent apoplexy.
Anxiety, downheartedness, moroseness, despondency, laziness, lassitude, and aversion to all kinds of work. θ Cholera.
Recurrence of feeling of impending evil.
Loud sobbing and weeping. θ Spinal irritation.
Delirium all night while lying quietly on his back. θ Typhus.
Furious delirium, with screaming and jumping out of bed.
Furious delirium at night, with great restlessness, followed by stupor in morning.
Delirium during heat.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Chin. s.]
Apathy, with stupid facial expression. θ Typhus.
Head heavy and giddy, he wants to lie down. θ Periodical cervical neuralgia.
Dizziness and enlarged feeling of head.
Whirling in head like a mill-wheel.
Vertigo, with buzzing in ears, difficult breathing, and sickness at stomach.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Chin. s.]
Frontal headache, where frontal bone verges towards top of head, a shaking pain, she feels every step, begins towards noon with chill.
Beating in vertex. θ Scarlatina.
Heaviness in head as from a cold. θ Cholera.
Intermittent neuralgia at regular hours.
Intermittent headache, violent throbbing, with vertigo and heat in face, involuntary closing of eyelids from sheer prostration.
Headache with nausea, chilliness, cold feet, great prostration. θ Menorrhagia.
Violent attacks of left-sided hemicrania occurring in evening.
Headache, the pain is not severe, but day after day, and week after week, the brain is one continued ache.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Chin. s.]
Distension of veins about head and neck. θ Puerperal convulsions.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Chin. s.]
Bright lights and sparks before eyes.
Black spot, size of pin's head, about eighteen inches from r. eye, and moving with eye, for some weeks.
Dimness of vision as from a net before eyes, and once as from a dark fog. θ Typhus.
Blindness ; amblyopia ; amaurosis.
Can only see objects when looking at them sideways.
Great sensitiveness of eye to light, with lachrymation in full glare of light.
Disk and retina both very anemic.
Eyes staring and lustreless. θ Spinal irritation.
Dilatation of pupils.
Supraorbital neuralgia occurring daily.
Neuralgic twinges in supra and infraorbital nerves generally periodic in character.
Intermittent strabismus ; child would squint one day and be entirely well on the next.
Conjunctiva injected, lids red and swollen, pupils contracted, lachrymation, extreme photophobia, tearing in orbit and headache, with thirst and fever ; all appearing every second day.
At 12 o'clock, daily, violent paroxysms of pain in and around left eye, conjunctiva inflamed, photophobia, pupil contracted, lachrymation, pressure > pain ; aggravation lasts until 8 P. M.
A sudden attack of violent pain above left eye, at 8 P. M., four days in succession, accompanied by slight delirium, muscular twitching and excessive sensitiveness to light and noise.
Violent stitching, throbbing pain in left eye, extending to forehead and temple, with photophobia, lachrymation, and inflamed conjunctiva, beginning at 1 P. M. daily, and lasting until 7, followed by perspiration. θ Intermittent.
Lancinating pain under right eye, commences at 7 A. M., lasting until after 3 P. M., when it disappears, leaving a sensation within cranium as if there was water dropping.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Chin. s.]
Ringing in ears, especially noticed in left, seldom in right.
Ringing as of bells. θ Spinal irritation.
Buzzing in ears. θ Typhus.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Chin. s.]
Violent epistaxis of young persons.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Chin. s.]
While writing sudden ache above left zygoma, also at temporal ridge.
Aching about left malar bone in evening.
Face pale and suffering, lips and nails blue.
Very pale, anxious face. θ Spinal irritation.
Jaundiced hue of face and conjunctivæ. θ Intermittent.
Face emaciated, stupid. θ Typhus.
Attacks of prosopalgia, occurring at 10 A. M., 3 P. M. and 10 P. M.
Right-sided prosopalgia daily, from 7 A. M. until noon, accompanied by fever and lachrymation of right eye ; the suffering parts become moist.
Facial neuralgia, morning periodicity, pains usually commence on left side, but sometimes on right side, and occasionally on both ; attacks commence every morning, and continue from 7 to 12 o'clock ; pains are lancinating, commence under eye, and soon extend into and around eye, causing considerable lachrymation ; pains > by pressure.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Chin. s.]
Swelling of submaxillary region. θ Variola.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Chin. s.]
Tongue and mouth dry ; bitter taste. θ Typhus.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Chin. s.]
Real thirst mostly only during sweat.
Excessive repugnance to all food.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Chin. s.]
Nausea and loathing of food. θ Cholera.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Chin. s.]
Pressure in pit of stomach up into throat, and pressure in stomach, < after drinking water. θ Cholera.
After eating, pressure in stomach, followed by cutting in upper and middle abdominal region.
Even the slightest food causes pressure in stomach and a return of the usual symptoms.
Dyspepsia or cardialgia, with nausea, loathing of food, bitter eructations, bitter taste in mouth, vomiting of bile, oppression of stomach, heartburn or burning in stomach and œsophagus, and feeling of constriction and pulling sensation in stomach.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Chin. s.]
Pain in region of liver, shortly before going to bed.
Severe pain in left hypochondrium, with shaking chill.
Pain in region of liver and spleen, on bending, taking a deep breath, or coughing. θ Intermittent.
Painful enlargement of spleen after intermittent.
Enlargement of spleen with dropsy.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Chin. s.]
Pain in bowels, especially after eating. θ Cholera.
Griping and tearing in abdomen, extending to chest, with pressing towards groin during menses. θ Dysmenorrhœa.
Abdomen distended. θ Typhus. θ Variola.
Visceral obstructions, especially engorgement of spleen and liver.
Cecal region distended, gurgling on pressure. θ Typhus.
Relaxed condition of digestive organs of old people, under the form of dyspepsia.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Chin. s.]
Nightly diarrhœa.
Constipation or soft stools followed by weakness.
Involuntary diarrheic stools. θ Typhus.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Chin. s.]
Urine fatty and deposits a straw-yellow, brick-dust sediment.
Involuntary urination. θ Typhus.
Albuminuria. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Urine loaded with lithates. θ Supraorbital neuralgia.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Chin. s.]
Profuse menstruation followed by headache, with nausea, chilliness, cold feet and prostration.
Passive metrorrhagias, with diminished irritability.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Chin. s.]
Two weeks after confinement, in consequence of fright, violent uterine neuralgia, returning at same hour every afternoon, accompanied by dyspnœa, small pulse, and clammy sweat on extremities, uterine region sensitive to touch.
The labor pains appear like tonic spasms, and are accompanied by convulsive twitches, unconsciousness after parturition, tetanic convulsions, in intervals convulsive action of muscles of face, eyes, etc. ; want of consciousness, oppressed respiration, distended veins on head and neck, weak, rapid and intermitting pulse, and albuminuria.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Chin. s.]
Can scarcely breathe from weakness. θ Intermittent.
Respirations 28. θ Variola.
Oppressed respiration. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Painful sense of pressure and weight on chest. θ Spinal irritation.
Anxiety and dyspnœa with intercostal pain. θ Typhus.
Respiration very much accelerated, abnormal rising and falling of thorax. θ Spinal irritation.
   

COUGH. [27] [Chin. s.]
Troublesome, moist cough. θ Variola.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Chin. s.]
Oppression of chest.
Stitches in left side, below short ribs.
Rattling of phlegm through entire right side of chest. θ Typhus.
Hemorrhage from lungs ; with diarrhœa, fever, cold sweat and prostration.
Pain in chest during chill.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Chin. s.]
Weak, rapid and intermitting pulse. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Pulse 100, very small, heartbeat not perceptible, sounds scarcely audible. θ Spinal irritation.
Pulse 120. θ Variola.
Palpitation from a little exercise.
   

OUTER CHEST. [30] [Chin. s.]
Stinging, tearing pain in intercostal space, between eighth and ninth ribs, right side, extending from spine to sternum, sensitive to pressure, < from 4 to 7 P. M., produces anxiety and dyspnœa. θ Typhus.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Chin. s.]
Every day at about 4 P. M. violent pain in lateral muscles of neck, which appear to him to be swollen and contracted, his head is giddy and heavy, and he wants to lie down. θ Periodical cervical neuralgia.
Sensitiveness of last cervical and first dorsal vertebræ to pressure.
Spine painful on pressure in all stages of fever paroxysm.
Three upper dorsal vertebræ are sensitive and painful to touch ; pressure causes dyspnœa. θ Spinal irritation.
Periodical pain in back, returning about midnight and extending into head. θ Spinal irritation.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Chin. s.]
Hands cold and cold sweat.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Chin. s.]
Sciatic neuralgia, on right side, of many weeks duration.
Acute rheumatic pain in left ankle joint after taking cold, accompanied by fever and profuse sweat.
Paralysis of lower extremities, involuntary stools and urination, occurring every other day during fever epidemic.
Paralysis of lower extremities, first occurring at 6 P. M., then half and hour earlier every day, with headache, chill, heat and sweat.
Cutting pains in feet during chill, ankles swollen.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Chin. s.]
Heaviness and aching in all limbs and especially in joints. θ Cholera.
Stiffness of nearly all joints, right wrist and knee joint very painful and much swollen. θ Acute rheumatism.
Acute articular rheumatism.
   

REST. POSITION. MOTION. [35] [Chin. s.]
Wants to lie down. θ Periodical cervical neuralgia.
   

NERVES. [36] [Chin. s.]
Great sensitiveness against external influences ; general weakness. θ Cholera.
Feels weak and nervous, a little exercise gives him palpitation.
Lassitude and inability to attend to his duties, has lost all zest for sport and exercise.
Debility caused by considerable losses of fluids ; particularly after weakening loss of blood.
General weakness, especially of feet.
Weakness and trembling in limbs and slow pulse.
Trembling in extremities ; the power of will over them seemed to be very much hampered.
Subsultus tendinum. θ Typhus.
Twitching, or clonic spasm in limbs. θ Spinal irritation.
Tetanic spasms with loss of consciousness during parturition and afterwards ; swollen veins on head and neck ; pulse frequent, intermittent and weak ; albuminuria.
Tetanic convulsions ; during intervals unconsciousness.
Intermittent neuralgia, pain return with great regularity.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Chin. s.]
Sleeplessness from over-stimulation of nervous system.
   

FEVER. [40] [Chin. s.]
Paroxysms ushered in with a mere transitory, at times almost imperceptible chilly feeling, principally across shoulders and nape of neck, up and down spine, lasting for a few moments only, occurring at different times throughout day.
Chill, regular paroxysms at same hour.
Decided shaking chill at 3 P. M.
During chill, blue lips and nails, ringing in ears, pale face.
Internal chilliness.
Chilliness, especially in back, alternating with flushes of heat. θ Cholera.
Chill every third day at 10 P. M., with intense thirst and pain in chest, followed by heat with headache, afterwards profuse perspiration ; little thirst during heat and sweat.
Chill every third day at 10 A. M., with cutting pains in feet, and swollen ankles.
Quartan ; chill at 4 P. M. ; chilly and hot flashes in alternation for an hour, introducing a high fever, which lasts all night, with profuse sweat ; during fever motion produces chilliness ; constant burning in stomach ; thirst satisfied for a moment with a swallow of cold water ; lips covered with colorless vesicles.
Quotidian ; chill at 8 A. M. ; chill, fever and sweat well marked, each lasting about two hours ; thirst for large draughts of cold water during whole paroxysm ; nausea continually and lasting till next chill.
Fever and ague, no symptoms during apyrexia except some lassitude ; paroxysms are regular and not attended with very obvious disturbances of any organ.
Distinct cold, hot and sweating stages, and perfect apyrexia.
Tertian ; chill at 12 o'clock, M. ; chill illy defined, lasting one-half hour, followed by intense fever, lasting ten hours, and terminating in scanty sweat ; constant frontal headache ; severe aching in limbs ; heat partially relieves all symptoms, particularly the chilliness.
Fever and ague with spinal irritation, cervical and dorsal vertebræ very tender to touch, pains in loins, thighs, and lower limbs generally, convulsive movements and jerks of single muscles, slight cramps, often only of muscles of left side, dyspnœa and oppression of chest, noises in ears with vertigo and dulness of mind.
Fever sets in about 6 P. M. and reaches its height about 10, continues until about 4 A. M., when sweat usually follows, with great prostration.
Fever with fulness in head, ringing in ears, together with hardness of hearing, dimness of vision, jaundiced hue of face and conjunctiva. θ Intermittent fever.
Sweat relieves all symptoms but headache, which is increased.
Debilitating sweat.
Typhus with great prostration, stupid facial expression, headache, diarrhœa, nosebleed, alternate chill and fever, aversion to move.
   

ATTACKS, PERIODICITY. [41] [Chin. s.]
Chill comes at 10 or 11 A. M. or between 3 and 10 P. M.
Stages of chill, fever and sweat well marked and distinct.
   

SENSATIONS. [43] [Chin. s.]
Internal bad feeling, as of coming illness. θ Cholera.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Chin. s.]
Great sensitiveness against external influences. θ Cholera.
   

SKIN. [46] [Chin. s.]
Confluent smallpox, eruption hemorrhagic ; pulse 120, respiration 28, abdomen distended but painless, submaxillary region swollen, moist, troublesome cough, great mental depression.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Chin. s.]
Cachectic persons weakened by loss of blood.
